newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PAPIN STILL HAS PLENTY TO OFFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PAPIN STILL HAS PLENTY TO OFFER.

text.p: Papinade may not be in the French dictionary but it is part of the soccer lexicon -- the name for Jean-Pierre Papin's trademark volleyed goals.
The usual Papinade involves the former French striker swivelling on his left foot to meet a cross on the turn and volley it into the net.

French first division pacesetters Paris St Germain were on the receiving end of a Papinade in a 5-3 mauling by Papin's new team Bordeaux recently, evidence that the 33-year-old is still as sharp as ever in front of goal.

Papin's return to French football this season after three years in exile is timely, not only in regenerating a talent which had appeared on the wane but also as a counterpoint to the exodus of many of the best of the next generation.

While the likes of Youri Djorkaeff, Christophe Dugarry and Nicolas Ouedec were heading for Italy or Spain, former AC Milan striker Papin was returning home from Bayern Munich to a league which looked in danger of losing its credibility.
Home, though, only in one sense, because he had made his name in the great Marseille side of the early 1990s and it appeared any other stage in France would not be good enough.
He had even once said, in the heat of competition, "the Girondins are the enemy, I would never play for Bordeaux".
But the Girondin fans warmed to his buoyant character and hard-work ethic and, as an example to the younger players in the team, he has been an astute signing by coach Rolland Courbis.
Papin recently praised "the intelligence of Rolland in managing his squad and those youngsters who are keen to show what they have in their bellies. It's great."
Courbis rested several first-choice players, including Papin, for the visit to Lens before the PSG clash and came home with a 4-3 victory. Three days later a fresher first string roasted the leaders.

Papin, top scorer in France three times between 1988 and 1991, has now scored eight goals as spearhead of a Bordeaux side who have become a realistic third member of a title-chasing trio with PSG and Monaco, the two favourites.
The 1991 European Footballer of the Year has found the net more than any of the other big-name French strikers still in the first division.
PSG's French international Patrice Loko, for one, is three goals short of Papin despite playing more often.

Papin, who dedicates all his spare time to his family and particularly his handicapped six-year-old daughter Emily, missed two matches in October to take the girl to the United States for specialist treatment.
His absence coincided with Bordeaux's first of four defeats so far this season. A month earlier they were top for 24 hours.
"It's a great moment in my career," Papin said after the victory over PSG. "Since 1986 with Olympique Marseille I hadn't lived such a moment of joy and emotion."

Papin made his French first division debut with two goals for Marseille in a 3-1 win over Monaco in August 1986, having joined them from Belgium's Brugge and played in the 1986 World Cup finals in Mexico. He scored 120 goals in 136 games in all competitions for Marseille before leaving for Milan in 1992.
"The people who brought me here (to Bordeaux) had confidence in me and I shall never be able to thank them enough," he said.
"We're convinced we can do something big this season...like believe in the title. We're certainly going to do our utmost to be party spoilers until the end of the season."

Such is Papin's standing in France that he is the only personality other than Brigitte Bardot to be known by his initials JPP which, instead of his full surname, the stocky blond striker wears over his club number 27 on the back of his Bordeaux jersey.
